title: U.S. House · Florida's 23rd District
area: Central and southern Palm Beach County, including West Palm Beach, under Florida's 2026 congressional map.

context.text: Florida's U.S. House elections use a new congressional map for 2026; Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the new district boundaries into law on May 4, 2026.
Incumbent Rep. Lois Frankel (D) won the Democratic primary on August 18, 2026, defeating Victoria Doyle and Mark Piper. Deborah Adeimy won the Republican primary, defeating Paola Branda.

summary.text: Lois Frankel is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for the 23rd District, first elected to the House in 2012 and now in her seventh term. A lawyer by training, she previously served in the Florida House of Representatives, including as minority leader, and as mayor of West Palm Beach. She sits on the House Appropriations Committee and is running for re-election.

background.text: Born in New York, New York, in 1948; earned a bachelor's degree in psychology from Boston University in 1970 and a J.D. from Georgetown University in 1973.
Worked as a lawyer before holding elective office.
Served in the Florida House of Representatives from 1986 to 1992 and 1994 to 2002, including as minority leader from 2000 to 2002.
Served as mayor of West Palm Beach from 2003 to 2011.
Won the Democratic nomination and the November 6, 2012 general election for the U.S. House, taking office in 2013; her official site describes her as in her seventh term.

Is a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, where she is the lead Democrat on the Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs and also serves on the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies Subcommittee.
Is Chair Emerita of the Democratic Women's Caucus and Co-Chair of the bipartisan Women, Peace, and Security Caucus, according to her official site.
Her official biography describes her as an avid abstract painter, the mother of a U.S. Marine veteran, and a grandmother of two.
Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 74.8% of the vote over Victoria Doyle and Mark Piper.

priorities.text: Says she is committed to lowering the cost of living, including groceries, gas, prescription drugs, and housing, and supported legislation letting Medicare negotiate drug prices.
Says she will always fight to protect Social Security and Medicare and opposes efforts to privatize Social Security or cut its benefits.
Says she is fully committed to restoring the right to abortion nationwide and co-leads the Women's Health Protection Act.

positions.summary: Says she is committed to restoring nationwide abortion rights and co-leads the Women's Health Protection Act.
positions.quote: I am fully committed to restoring the right to abortion nationwide.

positions.summary: Backs further gun-violence legislation including universal background checks, an assault weapons ban, and red-flag laws, and supported the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.
positions.quote: I will continue to fight for further legislation to reduce gun violence, including measures to require safe storage of firearms, require universal background checks, create an Office of Gun Violence Prevention, prohibit “ghost guns” (guns without serial numbers), ban assault weapons and high capacity magazines, eliminate gun manufacturers’ liability immunity, and establish federal extreme risk protection orders (“red flag laws”).

positions.summary: Says all Americans deserve access to affordable, quality health care and has worked to strengthen and expand ACA coverage.
positions.quote: I believe all Americans deserve access to affordable, quality health care, and I am fighting back hard against Republicans’ efforts to rip away health care for millions of families.

positions.summary: Says border enforcement officers need adequate tools and resources, while opposing the Trump administration's expanded enforcement actions such as ending TPS and reversing birthright citizenship, and supporting a pathway to citizenship.
positions.quote: At the same time, our border enforcement officers must have the tools and resources they need to keep us all safe and secure.

positions.summary: As Ranking Member of the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Subcommittee, says she supports continued security assistance to Israel and funding for its missile-defense capabilities.
positions.quote: In Congress, as Ranking Member of the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Subcommittee, I support continued security assistance to Israel and robust funding for Israel’s missile defense capabilities.

positions.summary: Supported the Inflation Reduction Act, which she describes as the most substantial legislation to combat climate change in the nation's history.
positions.quote: I am also proud to have supported the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), the most substantial legislation to combat climate change in our nation’s history.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations for the 2025–2026 Congress; previously served on the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (2017–2018) and the Committee on Veterans' Affairs (2021–2022).

summary.text: Deborah Adeimy is a financial services professional running as the Republican nominee against incumbent Lois Frankel. According to her Candidate Connection survey, she has worked as an advisor at major financial firms and is a Certified Financial Planner. She previously ran in the 2022 and 2024 Republican primaries for Florida's 22nd District and is campaigning on immigration enforcement, opposing tax increases, and a strong military.

background.text: Born in West Palm Beach, Florida; describes herself as a fourth-generation Floridian, daughter, mother and businesswoman.

In her 2021 survey she lists attending Cardinal Newman High School, Palm Beach State, and Loyola University, and earning a BSBA in finance from Thomas Edison University; she also lists completing Florida Atlantic University's Business Executive program.

Says she has worked as a strategic advisor at Merrill Lynch, Citi Global Markets and Morgan Stanley, holds multiple FINRA credentials, is licensed by the Florida Department of Financial Services for life and health insurance, and passed the CFP Board exam to become a Certified Financial Planner.

Lists memberships in the Historical Society of Palm Beach County, the Judeo Christian Republican Club, Dress for Success, the Republican Club of Palm Beach, the Norton Museum of Art and the Palm Beach Civic Association.
Ran in the 2022 Republican primary for Florida's 22nd District, finishing second with 34.3% of the vote, about 130 votes behind Dan Franzese.
Ran again in the 2024 Republican primary for Florida's 22nd District, finishing third with 22.2% of the vote.
Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary for the 23rd District with 73.7% of the vote over Paola Branda.
Says she is the mother of twin sons and a third child.

priorities.text: Says uncontrolled immigration threatens Americans' safety and calls for stronger immigration control.
priorities.quote: IMMIGRATION to America is to join and give and strengthen NOT divide and take and weaken. Chaotic tidal waves of immigrants threaten Americans' safety.

priorities.text: Opposes pending increases to individual income, capital gains, and corporate taxes.
priorities.quote: TAXES: Pending tax increases on American's income, capital gains and Corporate taxes will again, have negative impact.

priorities.text: Supports a powerful U.S. military and strengthening alliance partnerships and space defense.

positions.summary: Describes current immigration levels as a threat to Americans' safety and calls for stronger controls.
positions.quote: Chaotic tidal waves of immigrants threaten Americans' safety.

positions.summary: Opposes pending increases to income, capital gains, and corporate taxes.
positions.quote: TAXES: Pending tax increases on American's income, capital gains and Corporate taxes will again, have negative impact.

researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for incumbent Lois Frankel are added separately by script. Deborah Adeimy's Candidate Connection survey dates to 2021, from an earlier campaign; cited only for general biography and stated priorities that remain consistent with her current campaign. Biography gaps: Frankel's official site gives no birth or education details (taken from Ballotpedia); Adeimy's education is self-reported in the 2021 survey with some institutions listed without locations or degrees, and her campaign site was not found.
